description: Frozen out-of-sample corpus for iteration 021. None of these twelve tasks appears in the seed, pilot, arithmetic-vocabulary, or iterations 016–020 broad workload.

predeclared_analysis.role: Primary broad-corpus comparison after the v0.3.154 checker-totality correction; not a transcript-tuning target.
predeclared_analysis.matrix: 12 tasks x 3 languages x 6 complete-bundle replicates = 18 fresh sessions and 216 judged task assignments
primary_outcomes: median reported tokens per assigned task
median elapsed seconds per assigned task
predeclared_analysis.reporting: Preserve every session, source, attempt, hidden judgment, token count, elapsed time, and failure signature.
predeclared_analysis.change_rule: Do not add syntax or compiler behavior from one task or transcript. A proposal requires recurrence across unrelated task families plus independent general usefulness, semantic consistency, and maintainability. Checker-totality defects may be fixed as correctness bugs without a token-benefit claim.
predeclared_analysis.instruction_rule: Use the proven 1,519-character Parley skill byte-for-byte. The one allowed instruction-compression experiment is closed.

tasks.title: Sorted unique numbers
tasks.statement: Read a non-negative integer N from the first input line, then read exactly N signed whole numbers, one per line. Print each distinct value once in increasing numeric order, joined by commas with no spaces. If N is zero, print one empty line.

tasks.title: Balanced brackets
tasks.statement: Read one input line containing only the six ASCII bracket characters `()[]{}`; the line may be empty. Print `yes` exactly when every opening bracket is closed by the matching type in correct nesting order. Otherwise print `no`.

tasks.title: Matrix diagonal difference
tasks.statement: Read a non-negative integer N from the first input line, then read exactly N times N signed whole numbers, one per line, in row-major order. Print the absolute difference between the sum of the main diagonal and the sum of the opposite diagonal. If N is zero, print `0`.

tasks.title: Word frequency table
tasks.statement: Read a non-negative integer N from the first input line, then read exactly N nonempty lowercase ASCII words, one per line. Count each word and print all distinct words in alphabetical order as `word:count`, joined by commas with no spaces. If N is zero, print one empty line.

tasks.title: Postfix expression evaluation
tasks.statement: Read a positive integer N from the first input line, then read exactly N tokens, one per line. Each token is either a signed whole number or one of `+`, `-`, `*`. The tokens form a valid postfix expression. Evaluate it using whole-number arithmetic and print the result. For subtraction, the second-from-top value is the left operand.

tasks.title: Sorted-list search queries
tasks.statement: Read a non-negative integer N, then N distinct signed whole numbers in strictly increasing order, one per line. Next read a non-negative integer Q and then Q query numbers, one per line. For each query print its 1-based position in the sorted values, or `0` if absent. Print the Q answers on one line joined by commas. If Q is zero, print one empty line.

tasks.title: Caesar letter shift
tasks.statement: Read an integer K from the first input line, where K is from 0 through 25. Read one lowercase ASCII text line next; it may be empty. Replace every letter with the letter K positions later in the alphabet, wrapping after `z`, and print the result.

tasks.title: Sparse vector dot product
tasks.statement: Read a non-negative integer N, then N lines describing the first sparse vector. Each line is `index value`, where index is a non-negative whole number, value is a signed whole number, and indexes are unique within a vector. Then read M and M lines for the second vector in the same format. Print the dot product: sum the products at indexes present in both vectors.

tasks.title: Polynomial value
tasks.statement: Read a non-negative degree D from the first input line. Then read exactly D plus 1 signed whole-number coefficients, one per line, from the highest-degree coefficient through the constant coefficient. Finally read a signed whole number X. Evaluate the polynomial at X using whole-number arithmetic and print the result.

tasks.title: Inventory ledger
tasks.statement: Read a non-negative integer N from the first input line, then read exactly N event lines. Each event is `name delta`, where name is a nonempty lowercase ASCII word and delta is a signed whole number. Start every name at zero and add its deltas. Print every name that appeared, in alphabetical order, as `name:balance`, joined by commas with no spaces. Include zero and negative balances. If N is zero, print one empty line.

tasks.title: Gregorian date validity
tasks.statement: Read a positive whole-number year, then a whole-number month, then a whole-number day, one per input line. Print `yes` if they form a valid Gregorian calendar date and `no` otherwise. A leap year is divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100. Months outside 1 through 12 are invalid.

tasks.title: Nearest pair gap
tasks.statement: Read an integer N from the first input line, where N is at least 2. Then read exactly N signed whole numbers, one per line. Print the smallest absolute difference between any two distinct input positions. Equal values are allowed and therefore may produce `0`.
